title: Sensitivity of Bayesian Network Structure Learning to Search Algorithms and Scoring Functions: A Comparative Study Across Three Healthcare Datasets
content: In this paper we examine the relative influence of structure learning algorithms and scoring functions in Bayesian networks for healthcare applications. We compare Hill Climbing, Tabu Search, and Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) using the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), Bayesian Dirichlet equivalent uniform (BDeu), and K2 scoring functions on three healthcare datasets. On the full data, all three algorithms produced almost identical structures under BIC (Structural Hamming Distance [SHD] = 0 or 1). Bootstrap results showed a different pattern: Hill Climbing and Tabu Search remained identical in almost all resamples (median SHD = 0.0), whereas GES differed more from both (median SHD = 3.0–7.0). Changing the scoring function substantially altered the structure in two datasets but not the third. Overall, scoring functions produced larger differences than algorithms (median SHD = 8.5 vs. 3.0), although these values combine bootstrap and full-sample comparisons. Checks using different redundancy weights and discretization levels did not change the main pattern. Scoring functions were generally the larger source of disagreement, while algorithm agreement was less stable under resampling. Further datasets are needed to assess whether these findings generalize.
